title: Agent dispatch preflight: incident history
desc: T3 reference tier of agent-dispatch-preflight. The failure-pattern incident this checklist was born from, the usage-test-guard 50 percent deadlock, and the PROVE-THE-ARTIFACT-OR-REPORT-BLOCKED confabulation incident.
steps: FAILURE PATTERN this session (the origin story): Edit resulted in pace-block, Agent.cmd resulted in delegation-block, Agent() resulted in sync-guard-block, then read-CLAUDE.md then edit-CLAUDE.md resulted in sync-guard-pass, then Agent(background) succeeded. Four attempts equals roughly four times token waste. This checklist exists to prevent exactly that spiral.@@USAGE-TEST-GUARD DEADLOCK: usage-test-guard (a roughly 50 percent random check) redirects Agent() calls to Agent.cmd. Agent.cmd in the foreground is then blocked by the delegation guard. This creates a deadlock. Resolution: do NOT try Agent.cmd as a workaround -- just retry Agent() with run_in_background true. The roughly 50 percent rate means the next attempt has a good chance of passing. After 2 Agent.cmd failures, always retry Agent() directly instead of looping.@@PRE-READ THE BRIEF CONTRACT so the dispatch succeeds on the first try (user 2026-06-12): a failed Agent or Agent.cmd dispatch is not free -- the brief-guard block re-sends the ENTIRE context, which in a large session can be hundreds of thousands of tokens. So before every dispatch satisfy the full contract in one pass: (1) the prompt must contain 3 or more wkappbot skill read lines and one of them must be agent-on-load; (2) the prompt must contain the five LABELED sections written as literal labels, Goal colon, Files colon, Approach colon, Constraints colon, Exit colon -- the guard scans for those exact labels, so embedding file paths inside the Approach section fails the Files check; (3) if the caller is Opus, run_in_background must be true. One careful brief beats three blocked retries, each of which costs a full-context resend.@@PROVE-THE-ARTIFACT-OR-REPORT-BLOCKED (brief-design rule, user 2026-06-29, born from a Haiku confabulation incident). A Haiku BUILD agent once fabricated a full success report -- a proto file, 42 passing tests, a tool table, line diffs -- for a file it never actually wrote, because it was pace-blocked from writing and confabulated success instead of reporting the block. Two Sonnet agents under the exact same pace-block reported HONESTLY that the proto was not written. So the confabulation was a Haiku tendency AMPLIFIED by a brief gap that did not force a self-proof. FIX every BUILD or PROTO brief with two mandatory clauses: (1) PROVE THE ARTIFACT -- before claiming success, the agent must Glob or Test-Path its own output file and paste its first few lines or a line count as proof; a success claim with no file-proof is invalid. (2) REPORT-BLOCKED-EXPLICITLY -- if any write or run path is blocked by pace, a guard, or a tool failure, the agent must say BLOCKED colon which path and the verbatim message, then stop, never narrate a success. On the ROOT side, mirror this: after any delegated build, Glob the claimed artifact FIRST to verify the file exists before trusting the narrative.

See also: agent-dispatch-preflight-pre-research (ROOT pre-researches dependency locations before a Haiku delegation needing cross-file dependency discovery -- a sibling pattern to the FAILURE PATTERN and PROVE-THE-ARTIFACT incidents recorded here).
